first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, which is a direct operational problem affecting activation funnel health. memory_31 and memory_86 both show that simplification and shortening onboarding durably improve completion and early adoption. While competitive pricing pressure is real, addressing the internal activation decline first will prevent compounding leakage. I'm verifying memory_73 (promotional pricing) to confirm whether that should be the defensive play instead, and memory_31 to ensure the signup simplification approach remains sound in current context. Simplifying onboarding targets the measurable activation decline with proven mechanism and should improve time-to-value, making the product more competitive regardless of pricing. This preserves long-term qualified revenue by strengthening product stickiness rather than competing on price, which risks margin erosion. A standard experiment this week can generate signal on completion lift; results will inform whether we need concurrent price intervention next cycle.
